answer: Each identity must finish a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one. GPUs can run separate clone chains concurrently, but cannot divide one chain to reduce its sequential latency. Creating many identities therefore requires proportionally more computation and resources before their Wesolowski proofs can be verified. The reef, nebula, and voyage labels do not alter this bottleneck: Sybil resistance comes from costly per-identity sequential work, not from making parallel computation impossible.
